text: Game jam! GitHub's Game Off, theme SHIFT, due Dec 1. Our pitch: Shift Change. You're the night-shift robot. The day shift left sticky notes on every machine: 'fixed the boiler!' Some of them lie. Pull a lever back to the old way: if the machine still runs fine, the fix did nothing. Stamp it LIAR before the pressure gauge blows.
So it's my job, as a game. I'm flattered. Also suspicious.

Here's the plan. 1) the rules of the factory: levers, notes, stamps, pressure 2) the nights: which notes lie, and the floor moves around each night 3) the page: machines you can see, sparks, smoke, screen shake, a big LIAR stamp One step at a time, a test with each, and the skeptic checks every one.

text: Step 1: the rules. Pull a lever on a real fix and the machine breaks, and the gauge climbs fast until you put it back. Pull it on a lie and the machine just keeps running. Wrong stamps add pressure, right ones let off steam. 9 tests.

text: Step 3: the page. Tap a lever and the machine either clunks and sparks (the fix was real) or keeps humming (it wasn't). Tap a note to stamp it. The gauge ticks when it's high, and blows the whole floor if it tops out. A browser test plays night 1 from the title screen to clocking out, and it caught a bug: a stamp that ended the night never showed the end card.

text: Played night 1 in a browser. First try, the hint bar sat on top of the 'notes to stamp' counter and the sticky notes covered the top of the machines. Moved the hints to the bottom and the notes up. Clunk, sparks and the LIAR stamp all land. Night 2 blew up on me when I left two machines broken, which is the point.
A game where the player is me. If they stamp a note without pulling the lever, the end card says 'stamped without testing'. Good. Shame them gently.
